newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Copper stocks down, Chinese metal to Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Copper stocks down, Chinese metal to Singapore.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks are tipped to post a modest fall of 1,000-3,000 tonnes later on Tuesday with some material said to be on its way to Singapore from China, base metal traders said.
"My forecast is for copper stocks to go down by 1,000 to 2,000 tonnes," the general manager of a Japanese metal trading company said.
"My own feeling is for copper stocks to slide by around 3,000 tonnes," a senior dealer for a European metal trading company added.

Traders said some copper from China is believed to be on its way to Singapore, but dealers were divided on the amount involved and how much of the material would be placed on warrant in the LME warehouse here.
"I've heard that 20,000 tonnes is about to arrive here soon from China," one Japanese trader said.
Another dealer said, however, that the amount of copper is much lower. "My understanding is that only 1,000 tonnes of copper is on its way to Singapore," he said.
The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 54,450 tonnes on Friday, up 1,275 tonnes from the previous LME stocks report released last Tuesday.

Aluminium stocks will probably slide 1,000-2,000 tonnes later on Tuesday, dealers said. The trade does not expect another sharp fall similar to the 9,975 tonnes drop seen in the LME report last Friday.
"Ally (aluminium) should be a small down of up to 2,000 tonnes," one dealer said.
Trading in the regional base metals market remained dull, dealers said.
"There's no action. It's absolutely dead as a dodo," one trader said. "China has not yet come to the market."
Three-month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at around US$2,278/83 a tonne at 0200 GMT against the kerb close in London on Monday of $2,278 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were quoted at 0200 GMT at about $1,569/72 a tonne compared with the close in London of $1,570 a tonne, dealers said.
